issue_context.title: Specify thread pool by default for the parallel iteration of queries
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

The existing parallel iteration strategy requires specifying a thread pool, generally through `Res<ComputeTaskPool>`, and then passing in the parameters via a closure. See https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/parallel_query.rs

## What solution would you like?

1. Implicitly fetch the `ComputeTaskPool` resource with each query. This is cloned during system initialization.
2. Rename the existing method to `par_for_each_manual` and so on.
3. Add an ergonomic method for `par_for_each` (and eventually `par_iter` and friends) which uses this task pool.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

We could instead create a global / static thread pool that is always used. This may be necessary for performance or ergonomics reasons, but should not be necessary.

## Additional context

We cannot deprecate the existing techniques, as other thread pools may be desired in niche situations.

Related to #2088.

Discussed with @cart on [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/742569353878437978/911771583603937340).

review_comments: This clone is going to cause a subtle bug if anyone tries to replace the compute pool during running. The par_for_each is going ignore the pool being replaced and continue to use the original compute pool.
The more I think about this, the less such an operation makes sense. Even more reason to make TaskPools global and initialized once instead of allowing arbitrary reconfiguration mid execution.
agreed, but since this is one of the objections against global task pools, I'm not sure we can merge this without more clarity there.

Thinking on this a bit more, this isn't too different from the status quo. You can already spawn a task, embed a clone of the TaskPool it's running on, and have it run forever. Replacing the resource would spawn a new TaskPool, but the former pool wouldn't be cleaned up. 

Is this a problem? Yes. Is it one solvable within this PR? No. Does integrating this into ECS exacerbate the issue? Probably. Is it worth blocking this change on it? I don't think so. However, in turn, we should prioritize reviewing and merging #2250 or some variant of it to address this issue.
The clone still appears to be present.

This clone is unavoidable. The one referred to above is inside `par_for_each_unchecked_manual`, which originally cloned the TaskPool before running the `scope`. This is the "perf impact on initialization" that was previously mentioned.
